rule: Colour-1 divider lines split the grid into quadrants. One quadrant holds a template: a colour-2 square block with coloured rectangular pieces attached. Around every lone 2-square in another quadrant, redraw the template: scale it by (target size)/(template block size) using floor sampling, mirror it left-right and/or up-down when the target is across the column and/or row divider, and align its 2-block onto the target. Paint only non-background cells and clip at the grid border.
scope: Infer a multicolour template from one quadrant, scale it to each target square, mirror by relative quadrant, align its square and clip at outer borders while preserving distinguishing information.
constraints: All three canonical pairs reconstruct exactly;1,000 independent archived-solver checks give1,000 distinct inputs.

authored_scope:
Supported:
- Random scenes with quadrant sides 7..22 (default 9..15) and non-square grids.
- The template may sit in any of the four quadrants, with 2 or 3 targets.
- Aligned mode: unit lattice f in 1..3, block of one unit. Target sizes 1..4, including identity, enlarging, fractional (3->2) and shrinking ratios.
- Fine mode: block 2 with single-cell pieces. Target sizes {2,4}, with at least one size-4 target.
- Outer-border clipping, with every colour visible and at least half of the attachment cells visible.
- Explicit fixture reconstruction with strict validation.

Placement bias toward the dividers is handled constructively. Target sizes are chosen first. Per-axis template extent budgets are then capped by the tightest target and by the template quadrant, and split into an inner extent and an outer extent. This guarantees that the innermost target position always shows a full, unambiguous stamp. Tight layouts therefore keep the requested mode instead of switching to another.

Deliberately not supported:
- Other background, divider or block colours.
- More than one divider row or column.
- Several targets in one quadrant.
- Target sizes above 4.
- Lossy resampling. Fine-mode s=1 or s=3 is rejected explicitly by the lossless check.
- Stamps that overflow a quadrant toward the dividers.
authored_constraints: Grid is (top+bottom+1) x (left+right+1) and at most 30 per side. The divider row is at index top and the divider column at index left, both colour 1.
Exactly one quadrant contains colours other than 4 and 2. That template has exactly one solid colour-2 square. Its pieces have distinct colours and each touches the block or an earlier piece.
Random templates are never symmetric under a left-right flip, an up-down flip or a 180-degree rotation.
Each other used quadrant contains exactly one lone solid 2-square. Unused quadrants are empty.
The template, the target squares and every painted stamp cell keep a one-cell gap from both dividers. Stamps can be clipped only at the outer border.
Scaling is exact: the scaled block is a solid s x s square with no stray 2s and no lost colour.
Scaling is lossless: there are no truncated rows or columns, and every row or column dropped while shrinking duplicates a sampled one.
Every template colour is visible in each stamp, and at least half of the stamp's attachment cells are visible.
Each stamp's visible cells differ from those of all three wrong mirror orientations.
Every output differs from its input, because every stamp shows at least one attachment cell.
Explicit scenes check the raw template_pos and patch bounds before cropping, and apply the same visibility, losslessness and orientation checks as random scenes.
